newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GOVT SAYS ADDS OWN MEMBER TO CEN BANK BOARD.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GOVT SAYS ADDS OWN MEMBER TO CEN BANK BOARD.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesday said it had approved a measure which allows it to appoint one of its members to the central bank's governing board.
In a short statement, the government said it had approved the measure and had decided to appoint Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik as its representative to the board.
The statement gave no further details.
Earlier on Tuesday, National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) Spokesman Ivan Paska told Reuters that NBS governor Vladimir Masar had intended the government's meeting.
However, he said that Masar had intended to propose its bank supervision department director, Tibor Kasiak, for government approval as a new board member.
Central bank officials were not immediately available to comment on why Kozlik, and not Kasiak was appointed to the board. It was not clear whether Kasiak's appointment was discussed at the meeting.

According to the act which sets out the guidelines for the central bank's operation, the government appoints board members and its two chief executive directors based on a proposal by the governor. The act also says the central bank should operate indepently from the government.
The President appoints the governor and two vice-governors, based on government proposals and with parliament's approval.
Last week, the government appointed former Deputy Finance Minister Jozef Magula as a board member upon Masar's proposal.
Local bankers have been watching for signs that appointment of new board members by the government could reduce the NBS's independence and lead to any policy changes.
Leading government officials, including Kozlik, have repeatedly criticised the NBS's tight monetary policy.
